48-Hour Website vs 7-Day Website: What Can You Actually Launch?

By Chronolyte · Updated 2026-10-19

See what fits a 48-hour landing-page launch versus a seven-day business website, with practical scope, pricing and approval requirements.

Speed is useful only when a website functions properly. Chronolyte offers an accelerated workflow for qualifying, ready-to-build websites, not a blanket promise for every software project.

48-hour landing-page launch

For straightforward pages, the first launch can be targeted in 48 hours after the project scope is approved and the client provides copy, logo, images, domain access and timely feedback. A starting project quote may begin at $199.

  • A single responsive page
  • Basic contact or lead form
  • Essential metadata and analytics setup when access is available
  • Mobile checks and publishing

Seven-day small-business website

For a small brochure website with supplied content and no complex systems, the target delivery is up to 7 days after prerequisites are complete. Starting quotes may begin at $499, with final price depending on the number of pages and integrations.

  • A clear navigation structure and core service pages
  • Responsive design
  • Contact paths and basic SEO setup
  • Review, testing and launch handover

What cannot reasonably be guaranteed in a week?

Custom e-commerce workflows, advanced booking platforms, regulated integrations, native mobile apps, and subscription SaaS systems require their own schedules. App store reviews, third-party approvals, domain propagation and delayed client feedback are outside a fixed build window.

How to prepare for a fast launch

  • Provide page copy, business details, logo and images
  • Confirm a single decision-maker
  • Share hosting and domain access securely
  • Consolidate feedback and approve scope before work starts
